subject: SLA remedies: request for termination rights and liquidated damages
messages:
From: Leah Kim <leah.kim@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Dayton <mark.dayton@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA remedies: request for termination rights and liquidated damages

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. As we dig into the procurement checklist and our compliance board review, two items keep coming up from Legal and Risk: 1) Pioneer must be able to rely on contractual remedies beyond service credits (specifically a fee-at-risk schedule and a limited termination right for repeated, uncured breaches), and 2) for certain regulated workloads we need liquidated damages language as an alternative where service credits do not sufficiently cover remediation costs.

I attached our redlines (Pioneer_SLA_Redlines_20261214.pdf) and a proposed termination schedule spreadsheet that shows how we think fee exposure should be phased depending on severity and repetition. High level asks:
- A fee-at-risk cap of up to 6 months of committed fees for sustained, repeated SLO failures (not for transient infra incidents).
- A termination right if the same Severity 1 or Severity 2 SLO is missed 3 times within a 90-day rolling window after the cure period.
- Liquidated damages for regulatory-impacting outages (we provided example language in the redlines).

We understand these are outside standard vendor terms; Pioneer is willing to negotiate limits, escrow of the at-risk fees, and a right-sized carve-out for force majeure and planned maintenance. Can you confirm whether Redwood would consider: (a) an escrow arrangement for fee-at-risk, (b) a formal cure period, and (c) a narrowly-scoped termination path tied to repeated material SLA violations?

Would like to schedule a short call with Legal and Sales Ops this week if possible — cc'ing Mark who is coordinating procurement.

Thanks,
Leah Kim
Head of IT Procurement
Pioneer Health

Attachments: Pioneer_SLA_Redlines_20261214.pdf, ProposedTerminationSchedule.xlsx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: SLA remedies: request for termination rights and liquidated damages

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Pioneer’s ask. They want fee-at-risk / escrow + termination on repeated SLO misses and even liquidated damages for regulatory-impact outages. Attached their redlines and the termination schedule.

My quick take: we should be pragmatic — avoid open-ended LDs, propose hard caps, strong cure periods, and limit termination to repeated, material breaches (and exclude customer-side misconfig/overuse). Marissa, can you draft a counterproposal that:
- offers an escrow mechanism or equivalent holdback for a capped sum (e.g., up to 6 months fees)
- replaces broad LD language with narrowly-scoped regulatory-impact clause (with high evidentiary bar)
- defines an explicit cure and escalation process and limits termination triggers to 3 qualifying events in 90 days

Also loop in Legal for any suggested wording. If we can push a compromise that preserves our risk profile, we can keep the deal moving.

Thanks — I’ll book a slot for Wed morning with Pioneer if you think we have something to show.

-jb
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 14:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA remedies: request for termination rights and liquidated damages

Jordan / Karthik —

Thanks for forwarding. I drafted a counterproposal and attached a redline with specific contract language (redwood_counter_sla_language.docx). Summary of proposed positions:

1) Fee-at-risk / escrow
- We're willing to accept a time-limited fee holdback up to a capped amount equal to 6 months of committed net fees but only applied to the specific SOW/project that experiences the repeated breaches.
- Funds to be held in escrow administered by a mutually-agreed escrow agent; release rules tied to mutually-agreed cure verification steps.

2) Termination rights
- Termination right granted only after: (a) the same Severity 1 or Severity 2 SLO is missed on 3 separate billing days within a 90-day rolling window, AND (b) Redwood fails to remediate within a 30-day cure period following written notice.
- Exclusions: incidents caused by Customer misconfiguration, force majeure, or Beta features explicitly opted-in by Pioneer.
- Termination remedies limited to pro-rated prepaid fees and the escrowed amount; no open-ended damages.

3) Liquidated damages (regulatory-impact clause)
- We will accept a narrowly-tailored LD clause for outages that demonstrably trigger regulatory reporting obligations for Pioneer, provided:
  a) the LD is a fixed, pre-agreed amount not to exceed the escrow cap, and
  b) triggering requires documented regulator communication and a joint incident review confirming Redwood causation.

4) Process and governance
- Add a 7-business-day preliminary technical investigation and 30-day cure period before escalation to legal.
- Add a joint monthly reliability review for the first 6 months post-launch.

I think this keeps us protected while giving Pioneer the commercial reassurance they want. Attached redline includes specific clause language and a proposed short-form SOW amendment. If you’re good with this, I can send to Pioneer legal with the redlines and a short cover note, and propose a Wed 11:00am PT call.

Marissa
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_counter_sla_language.docx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Leah Kim <leah.kim@pioneerhealth.com>, Mark Dayton <mark.dayton@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, LegalOps <legalops@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA remedies: request for termination rights and liquidated damages

Leah / Mark —

Appreciate the clear framing and the spreadsheet — helped us move quickly. Attached (Pioneer_SLA_Redlines_v2.pdf) is our initial redline and a one-page summary of the compromise Marissa outlined. High-level offer:

- We can agree to an escrow-style fee holdback capped at 6 months of committed fees for the affected SOW, administered by a neutral escrow agent with pre-agreed release rules.
- Termination right: limited to 3 qualifying SLO misses in a 90-day window AND failure to cure within 30 days. Exclusions for customer-caused incidents and force majeure included.
- Liquidated damages: we will accept a narrow LD trigger for regulator-notifiable outages, but the LD is capped at the escrow amount and requires documented regulator contact plus a joint incident causation finding.
- Governance: 7-business-day technical investigation, 30-day cure period, and monthly reliability reviews for 6 months after launch.

We believe this addresses Pioneer’s key concerns while keeping the remedy exposure bounded. If you’re aligned, Marissa can circulate the redline into your markups and we can take the proposed Wednesday 11:00am PT call to run Legal and finalize wording. If Pioneer prefers, we can also prepare a short DocuSign change-order that captures the escrow and termination schedule — I’ve included a link to the draft envelope for quick signature.

Call options: Wed 11:00am PT or Thu 08:00am PT — what works for you?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this piece so we can move to onboarding.

-jb
Redwood Inference
